# What OpenBao must grant

<!-- Generated by `mix troupe.openbao.policy` from `Troupe.KMS.Policy.plane_grants/1`.
     Do not edit: the plane checks the same list against its own token. -->

The plane cannot write its own policies. That takes an OpenBao administrator, a root
token or one allowed to write `sys/policies/acl` and the auth roles, which the plane
never is. So an administrator runs the lines below once, and again for a grant an
upgrade adds; nothing else here is done by hand.

**The plane checks them.** When it starts, and on the console's Overview, the plane asks
OpenBao what its own token may do at each path below, look-only
(`sys/capabilities-self`, which the `default` policy allows), and says in one sentence
for each grant it lacks what fails without it, with the lines that grant it, written
with the deployment's own mounts, key names, role and the policies its token already
carries. `admin.overview` answers the same as `openbao`.

The names are the defaults: mounts `secret` (KV v2) and `transit`, the Kubernetes auth
mount `kubernetes`, the role `troupe-plane` (the chart's `bao.authPath` and
`bao.planeRole`), and the release namespace `troupe-system`.

## 1. Before the plane starts

The engines, the session-token key, Kubernetes auth with a reviewer
([integrations.md §2](integrations.md#2-openbao)), and the plane's role, carrying the
policy of every grant the plane needs:

```sh
bao secrets enable -path=transit transit
bao secrets enable -path=secret -version=2 kv
bao write -f transit/keys/troupe-session-tokens type=ecdsa-p256
bao auth enable kubernetes
bao write auth/kubernetes/config kubernetes_host=https://kubernetes.default.svc:443   # and the reviewer's JWT and CA
bao write auth/kubernetes/role/troupe-plane bound_service_account_names=troupe-plane bound_service_account_namespaces=troupe-system audience=troupe-kms token_policies=troupe-plane-session-tokens,troupe-plane-signing,troupe-plane ttl=1h
```

Then write each policy in section 2. A plane whose role is missing or refuses its
ServiceAccount token says so at start, and on the Overview, with the role line above.

## 2. What the plane's role carries

| grant | policy | what it is for | without it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session-tokens` | `troupe-plane-session-tokens` | sign session tokens, and read the key's public half that workers check them with | no session opens, and no pod or person's daemon can check a token |
| `plane-signing` | `troupe-plane-signing` | make, rotate and sign with the plane's own key, which signs what it tells people's machines | the client versions and defaults go out unsigned, and every client that pinned this plane's key refuses them |
| `erasure` | `troupe-plane` | destroy an erased session's key, a team's or a person's, and see which credentials a person has connected | erasing a session cannot destroy its key, and the console cannot say who has connected what |
| `github-app` (only with a GitHub App) | `troupe-plane-github` | import, sign with and delete the GitHub App's key and webhook secret | a GitHub App cannot be set up, and one set up before stops signing |

### `troupe-plane-session-tokens`

To sign session tokens, and read the key's public half that workers check them with.

```sh
bao policy write troupe-plane-session-tokens - <<'POLICY'
path "transit/sign/troupe-session-tokens" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-session-tokens" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
POLICY
bao write auth/kubernetes/role/troupe-plane token_policies=troupe-plane-session-tokens,troupe-plane-signing,troupe-plane
```

### `troupe-plane-signing`

To make, rotate and sign with the plane's own key, which signs what it tells people's machines.

```sh
bao policy write troupe-plane-signing - <<'POLICY'
path "transit/keys/troupe-plane-signing" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-plane-signing/rotate" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

path "transit/sign/troupe-plane-signing" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}
POLICY
bao write auth/kubernetes/role/troupe-plane token_policies=troupe-plane-session-tokens,troupe-plane-signing,troupe-plane
```

### `troupe-plane`

To destroy an erased session's key, a team's or a person's, and see which credentials a person has connected.

```sh
bao policy write troupe-plane - <<'POLICY'
path "secret/metadata/troupe/teams/+/sessions/*" {
  capabilities = ["delete", "list", "read"]
}

path "secret/metadata/troupe/people/+/sessions/*" {
  capabilities = ["delete", "list", "read"]
}

path "secret/metadata/troupe/people/+/mcp/*" {
  capabilities = ["list", "read"]
}
POLICY
bao write auth/kubernetes/role/troupe-plane token_policies=troupe-plane-session-tokens,troupe-plane-signing,troupe-plane
```

### `troupe-plane-github`

To import, sign with and delete the GitHub App's key and webhook secret. Only where the plane has a GitHub App.

```sh
bao policy write troupe-plane-github - <<'POLICY'
path "transit/wrapping_key" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-app" {
  capabilities = ["read", "delete"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-app/config" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-app/import" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-app/import_version" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/sign/troupe-github-app" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-webhook" {
  capabilities = ["read", "delete"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-webhook/config" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-webhook/import" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/keys/troupe-github-webhook/import_version" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}

path "transit/hmac/troupe-github-webhook/sha2-256" {
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]
}
POLICY
bao write auth/kubernetes/role/troupe-plane token_policies=troupe-plane-session-tokens,troupe-plane-signing,troupe-plane,troupe-plane-github
```

## 3. Workers and people

Their roles are not the plane's, and the plane cannot check them: a worker pod logs in
as `troupe-worker` (or a role per profile), and a person's daemon at the `jwt` auth mount
as `troupe-person`. Their policies and roles are in
[roles-and-permissions.md §8](roles-and-permissions.md#8-openbao-policies), rendered by
the same module.
